title: QBR - Halcyon AI Health Check
summary: Quarterly health check focused on rising token usage, cost optimization options (caching, batching, quantization), reliability incidents and SLOs, and potential pilot of Dedicated capacity. Agreed next steps: share updated cost dashboard, schedule technical deep dive + benchmark next week, provide SOC2 and VPC/KMS docs, proposal for a 90-day Dedicated pilot.
meeting_header: Date: 2026-12-06 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 45 mins | Attendees: Ava Chen, Diego Ramos, Priya Nair (Redwood) — Gina Park, Leo Martinez, Sofia Ruiz, Tom Becker (Halcyon AI)
transcript: 00:00 Ava Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining the QBR, appreciate you blocking time today.
00:08 Gina Park: Thanks Ava, yeah we wanted to walk through usage, costs, and where we're at for next quarter.
00:16 Priya Nair: Quick agenda — usage trends, reliability incidents, security questions, roadmap asks, and next steps. Is that okay?
00:23 Leo Martinez: Yep that sounds good. We also want to see the cost breakdown for embeddings — that's spiking for us.
00:31 Diego Ramos: Cool. I'll pull up the dashboard. Quick note: some of my slides say Redwood Dedicate — that's a dumb transcribe typo in the notes, we mean Redwood Dedicated capacity.
00:45 Tom Becker: On reliability side we had a couple of tail latency spikes last month — two incidents around 03:00 UTC that affected our inference pipeline.
00:53 Diego Ramos: Right, I have the incident timeline here — looks like an autoscaler edge case plus a model fallback that added latency. We fixed the policy post-mortem.
01:05 Sofia Ruiz: Can you remind us what the SLOs are for hosted versus dedicated? We need that for our compliance report.

01:13 Ava Chen: Hosted API target SLO is 99.5% availability and median p99 latencies of 300-500ms depending on the model family; Dedicated has SLA options and more predictable p99s, typically sub-200ms for our standard models.
01:28 Gina Park: Okay, good. On usage we saw a 38% month over month increase — mainly from chat completions and embedding calls for semantic search.
01:36 Priya Nair: Do you know the distribution — is it user-driven chat or backend batch embeddings?
01:41 Leo Martinez: It's mixed. User chat is up 22%, but embeddings batch jobs are up 75% — those nightly reindexes for search and recommendations.
01:51 Diego Ramos: That aligns with what the cost dashboard shows — embeddings are the dominant line item. We can look at quantization and batching to lower unit cost for those workloads.
02:05 Tom Becker: For embeddings, is there a recommended cache pattern? We have a lot of repeated queries that could be cached at the prefix level.
02:12 Diego Ramos: Yes — we recommend a hybrid approach: local caching for hot keys plus Redwood prefix/KV cache for cross-instance hits. Note my notes sometimes say KV cash, but it's KV cache.
02:24 Gina Park: Sounds good, does that add latency? We need sub-100ms for some endpoints.

02:29 Diego Ramos: Local cache typically returns sub-5ms; prefix/KV cache adds low single-digit ms but significantly reduces token count to the model so cost goes down and often end-to-end latency improves.
02:45 Sofia Ruiz: Security question — for the Dedicated pilot we want VPC peering and KMS integration. Do you support customer-managed keys and audit logs?
02:53 Ava Chen: Yes, Dedicated and Private options support customer KMS/HSM keys, and we stream audit logs to your SIEM. We'll share the SOC 2 audit pack and the VPC network diagram after this call.
03:07 Leo Martinez: Great. On the incidents you mentioned earlier — were those related to model fallback and scaling? We want to avoid noisy fallbacks during peak minutes.
03:15 Diego Ramos: It was a combination — scale-up race condition and an aggressive fallback policy that swapped to a larger variant. We tuned autoscaler cooldowns and adjusted fallback thresholds.
03:28 Gina Park: Any recommended configuration changes on our side?

03:31 Diego Ramos: We'll propose an autoscaler policy tailored to your traffic patterns and a fallback plan that prioritizes smaller-variant fallbacks first. Also, consider pinning model versions during critical windows.
03:44 Priya Nair: A few customers we've seen benefit from scheduled warm pools to avoid cold-start latency for predictable batch jobs — is that something you can automate?
03:52 Diego Ramos: Yes, we have warm pool suggestions in Redwood Optimize; we can create a policy that spins up minimal reserved workers before your nightly reindex starts.
04:02 Tom Becker: For the embeddings cost — can you run a quick estimate if we quantize the model and move to int8?
04:08 Diego Ramos: Short answer: you could get 30-45% cost reduction depending on the model and acceptable quality delta. We'll run a short eval with your prompts to measure quality impact.
04:20 Leo Martinez: That would be super helpful — quality regressions are the major blocker for us adopting more aggressive quantization.
04:26 Diego Ramos: Totally. We'll use your eval set and report on ROUGE/semantic sim changes. Note there might be small transcription errors in the eval names in my notes.
04:38 Gina Park: Roadmap asks — we plan to onboard more EU customers Q1 and need data residency and region routing. Can Redwood route by region automatically?
04:45 Ava Chen: Yes, smart routing can pin requests to region and fallback to a secondary if there's an outage. We'll document the routing policy and region availability matrix for you.
04:57 Sofia Ruiz: Any compliance blockers for EU data residency with your hosted API?
05:01 Ava Chen: For EU residency we recommend Dedicated or Private; hosted can be regionally constrained but Dedicated gives you guaranteed isolation and contractual controls.
05:10 Leo Martinez: Pricing question — how does the Reserved Dedicated pilot billing work? We want a 90-day trial with predictable monthly caps.
05:17 Ava Chen: We can do a usage + reserved blend: commitment for baseline capacity with monthly true-up for burst. We'll send a formal pilot proposal with numbers.
05:27 Priya Nair: Also we'll include a playbook for rollback and canary deploys during the pilot so your team can run A/Bs safely.
05:35 Gina Park: Perfect. Next, are there any performance benchmarks we should run ourselves during the deep dive?
05:40 Diego Ramos: We'll propose a benchmark harness: representative prompts, sequence lengths, and concurrency to mimic your peak. We'll also run a KV cache enabled/disabled comparison.
05:51 Tom Becker: Can we run that in our VPC with a private deployment or do you need to run it in Redwood environment?
05:57 Diego Ramos: We can run both: a Redwood-hosted benchmark for fastest results and a private/VPC run for a like-for-like comparison. The VPC run requires some infra prep — we'll include steps.
06:09 Leo Martinez: Timing — when can we do the technical deep dive? Next week would be ideal.
06:14 Ava Chen: How about Thursday 2026-12-10 at 14:00 UTC? We'll get Diego and an infra engineer in the session.
06:20 Gina Park: Works for us.
06:22 Priya Nair: I'll send the invite and include the benchmark spreadsheet. Sorry if some names in the notes are mangled, my auto-transcript is weird sometimes.
06:31 Sofia Ruiz: Action items on security: send SOC2 pack, VPC diagram, and KMS integration doc. We'll review and flag any gaps.
06:39 Ava Chen: We'll also send an initial Dedicated pilot SOW and a cost estimate for quantization and caching changes.
06:46 Leo Martinez: One last thing — can you add a per-route token burn metric to the dashboard? We want to see token/req and cost per route.
06:54 Diego Ramos: Yep, per-route breakdown is available. We'll add Token Burn + Cost/Route into the dashboard and share a link.
07:02 Gina Park: Great — thanks everyone. Recap and next steps please?

07:07 Priya Nair: Recap: send SOC2 & security docs, share updated cost dashboard with per-route metrics, schedule tech deep dive on 2026-12-10, provide Dedicated pilot SOW and cost estimate, run quantization eval with your prompt set. Any other items?
07:21 Tom Becker: That's it for me, thanks.
07:23 Ava Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the materials and invite. Bye.
45:00 [call ended]
